title: Slab-based parallelization for rerank + soft timeouts and token budget enforcement
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce p95/p99 latency and unit cost for the reranking endpoint under mixed-length candidate sets by introducing a slab-based parallel execution model, soft (graceful) timeouts, and per-request token budgets. Motivation: existing single-stream rerank handling suffers from long tail when a few candidates have very long token lengths or slow kernel paths; batching across unrelated requests also increases variance. Approach summary:

1) Slab-based parallelization: group rerank candidates into 'slabs' by estimated token length (short / medium / long) and schedule independent worker shards for each slab so that short candidates are not blocked by long ones. Slabs are created per-request but workers are pooled to reuse compiled kernels. This keeps KV-cache locality for similar-length work and enables independent micro-batching within slabs.

2) Soft timeouts & token budgets: implement a two-tier timeout system: a conservative hard deadline for SLA safety and a soft deadline that triggers graceful truncation and a quality-aware fallback (score normalization + early stopping). Each rerank request carries a token_budget hint (derived from client service plan or default heuristic). When a slab exceeds its budget, we prioritize completing smaller candidates and emit a 'partial_scores' flag in the response so callers can request a low-latency re-rank if needed.

3) Deadline-aware priority queuing: requests get a priority score computed from (remaining_time_budget, customer_tier, request_age). The scheduler uses this to form micro-batches respecting per-shard deadlines; if a higher-priority request arrives, we perform lightweight preemption by draining current micro-batch before scheduling the new one.

4) Non-blocking KV-cache refreshes: avoid synchronous KV cache fills for long sequences by making cache population async; cold-cache misses return estimates computed from smaller context and enqueue a background cache fill to improve follow-up requests.

Benchmarks (internal perf run 2025-02-18, variant: rerank-std with 12 candidates, mixed token lengths 8/32/256):
- Baseline p95: 420ms, p99: 890ms
- Slab + soft-timeout prototype p95: 210ms, p99: 480ms (approx 50% p95 reduction)
- End-to-end throughput improvement: +28% aggregated across mixed workloads
- Unit cost: ~7% reduction due to fewer wasted long-path cycles and better micro-batching utilization

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Quality regressions for clients relying on full-token reranks: mitigated by partial_scores flag and an opt-out header to force full evaluation (incurs latency). We need to document behavior and provide SDK support for incremental rerank calls.
- Complexity increase in scheduler & observability: added metrics and traces are required; see observability TODOs below.
- Preemption fairness and starvation: prototype uses aging to avoid starvation but needs more stress testing for pathological burst patterns.

Design & API changes:
- New request fields: token_budget (int, optional), allow_partial (bool, optional), slab_hint (enum optional for advanced clients)
- Response additions: partial_scores (bool), missing_candidates (list of candidate ids) when partial, slab_diagnostics (string url)
